items.title: Rob Mounsey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 9, 2025
items.q: they called me in to play the piano solo... Donald Fagen said... just play, comp a little bit through the rest of the track

ctx.x: Yes Zoom doesn’t really like it, but yes I’m a huge Steely Dan fan, yeah.

Well there’s a piano solo and they called me in to play the piano solo. This was Automated Beat in New York. It must have been 1982 I think. And you know they were famously, famously very, very exacting which nobody ever minded because everybody loved the music and loved the songs. And we got the piano solo in a couple of hours, maybe two hours, which is pretty good for them. Two punches, it’s 12 bars, we carefully made that. And then to my surprise Donald Fagen said, “And now we just need you to © Fillius Jazz…

just play, comp a little bit through the rest of the track because we don’t want the piano to just appear out of nowhere, we want it to kind of be part of the band so just —.” Okay that didn’t sound too difficult so they played the track and the song, if you remember it, is very harmonically strange. It’s very harmonically unsettled. It’s sort of constantly making left turns.
